## Finding

In trunk a guard that names this ticket disables `tests/dynamiccstructret.c.in` for mcs51 with
`--stack-auto`. After the guard is removed, the test fails on r17158 for mcs51-small-stack-auto
and mcs51-large-stack-auto. The failure does not depend on `__dynamicc`. It occurs when the caller
pushes a struct argument by value while r0 and r1 both hold values that are needed later.

## Cause

`genPointerPush` in `src/mcs51/gen.c` generates the code for `IPUSH_VALUE_AT_ADDRESS`, which pushes
a struct argument byte by byte. When the struct is addressed through a one-byte pointer,
`genPointerPush` requests a pointer register from `getFreePtr`. When r0 and r1 are both in use,
`getFreePtr` saves one of them. For `IPUSH` and `PCALL` it copies the register to B. For every
other operation it pushes the register, and in trunk `IPUSH_VALUE_AT_ADDRESS` is one of the other
operations.

The byte that `getFreePtr` pushes is then on the stack below the argument bytes. `genPointerPush`
calls `freeAsmop` with `pop` false, so no instruction removes it. After the call, the caller pops
its registers from positions that are one byte too high, and the stack pointer stays one byte
above its value before the call sequence.

## Fix

`getFreePtr` treats `IPUSH_VALUE_AT_ADDRESS` as it treats `IPUSH` and `PCALL`. It copies the
register to B, and `freeAsmop` restores it with `mov r0,b` or `mov r1,b`. The loop in
`genPointerPush` that pushes the bytes uses only A and the pointer register. The patch also removes
the guard from the test.

## Verification

After the guard is removed, `tests/dynamiccstructret.c.in` fails for mcs51-small-stack-auto and
mcs51-large-stack-auto without the patch and passes for both with it.

## Related

Bug #3395 is the failure of `gte/pr30185.c` for the two stack-auto targets. That test passes with
this patch.
